title: Reaching Without a Formula: The Jacobian, Measured

questions.question: How do you get the Jacobian of an arm nobody has derived a formula for?
options: Invert the forward kinematics
It cannot be obtained without a formula
Derive it symbolically from the link parameters
Measure it: nudge each joint, see how the tool moved, divide by the nudge
questions.explanation: Which is why a numerical solver does not care what shape the arm is, including one whose geometry came out of a file this morning.

questions.question: Measured against an exact derivative, which finite difference step was most accurate?
options: The largest one tried, 1e-1
The smallest one tried, 1e-14
They were all within an order of magnitude
About 1e-6, with 1e-14 being worse than 1e-1
questions.explanation: Truncation error falls as the step shrinks and rounding error rises, so there is a best step in the middle. Making it smaller past that point makes the answer worse.

questions.question: Why does the Jacobian transpose method need no matrix inverse?
options: It solves the system by elimination instead
Each joint moves by the dot product of its own column with the error, which is how much moving it would help
The Jacobian of a serial arm is always orthogonal
It uses the inverse of the transpose, which is cheaper
questions.explanation: It is the simplest method that works and it is not the fastest. What it buys is that every line of it can be read.

questions.question: A target outside the workspace is given to an iterative solver with no iteration cap. What happens?
options: It returns an error
It returns the nearest reachable point
It never returns: the error stops going down and nothing in the arithmetic notices
It oscillates and then converges
questions.explanation: There is no exception, no special value and no signal. The loop is still doing its job, and its job has no end.

questions.question: The solver runs out of iterations. What should it return?
options: The best angles it found, the error it reached, the iteration count, and the fact that it did not converge
An empty result, since the answer is not valid
The angles, since they are the best available
The starting angles, unchanged
questions.explanation: The angles are useful as a starting point or something to show on a screen. What they are not is a command, and only the flag separates them from one.

questions.question: Approaching the workspace edge, convergence went 390 then 1281 then 5236 iterations, then failed. What is that?
options: The singularity from lesson 13-02, seen from the solver's side: the columns line up and the direction outward stops existing
A sign that the gain is too small
The iteration cap being reached by chance
Accumulated rounding error in the Jacobian
questions.explanation: The same geometry that made the closed form's two answers merge is what makes the numerical method stall. Convergence slowing sharply is how it announces itself before it stops working.
